draft.text: You came in because you have been having swelling and pain in your right leg, especially around your knee, for about two months.
The swelling has gotten worse and now affects your whole leg.
We found that your leg is swollen and sore when pressed.
You also have warmth and tenderness around your knee.
There is no redness or signs of infection.
Your symptoms may be related to your rheumatoid arthritis.
This is a condition that causes joint pain and swelling, and it can affect other parts of the body.
You will need more tests, like imaging of your knee and leg, to check for problems like fluid buildup or other issues.
You should keep taking your medicines and talk to your doctor about these next steps.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been having swelling and pain in your right knee for two months.
The pain has gotten worse and now affects your whole leg, especially around the knee.
You described the pain as usually around a 6 on a normal day, but it has decreased to a 3 lately.
You have no fever, weight loss, or fatigue.
You feel warmth and tenderness around the knee, but no redness.
You sit for long periods during the day, which may contribute to the swelling.
Your symptoms are consistent with your ongoing rheumatoid arthritis.
The swelling and pain in your knee and leg may be related to your RA.
You have not had any recent imaging or blood tests to check the cause of the swelling.
You will be referred for further evaluation, including imaging studies like an ultrasound or MRI of your right knee and leg.
You will also have blood tests to check for infection or inflammation.
You should continue taking your current medications and follow up with your doctor for further evaluation and management.
